```{python}
#| code-fold: true
from pathlib import Path
import urllib.request

DATA = Path("../../data")
if not DATA.exists():
    DATA = Path("data")
    DATA.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    base = ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tlorans/"
            "kiku-value-premium-replication/main/data/")
    for f in ("annual_panel.csv", "consumption_annual.csv", "rf_annual.csv"):
        if not (DATA / f).exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(base + f, DATA / f)
```

## Table II solution

The default model is the paper's calibration. `method="analytical"`
reads loadings, and the grid is the paper's quantitative solution.

```{python}
import geap
from great_tables import GT

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")

model = geap.LongRunRisksModel()
print(model.solve(method="analytical").summary())
```

```{python}
res = model.solve()
print(res.compare("value", "growth", market="market").summary())
```

## Two firms that differ only in $\phi$

```{python}
import pandas as pd

BASE = dict(mu=0.0015, phi_sigma=7.5, alpha=0.5)
firms = geap.LongRunRisksModel(
    claims={"A": dict(BASE, phi=0.5), "B": dict(BASE, phi=1.5)},
).solve(method="analytical")

names = list(firms.claims)
rows = pd.DataFrame({
    "firm": names,
    "phi": [firms.params.claims[n].phi for n in names],
    "a1": [firms.A1[n] for n in names],
    "prem": [firms.long_run_premium[n] for n in names],
})
(
    GT(rows)
    .tab_header(title="Two firms that differ only in the loading")
    .cols_label(firm="firm", phi="phi", a1="A1", prem="long-run premium %")
    .fmt_number(columns="phi", decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="a1", decimals=1)
    .fmt_number(columns="prem", decimals=2)
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

Firm B tracks the persistent component, so $A_1$ is positive. The
long-run premium is therefore positive. Firm A's loading is below
$1/\psi = 0.67$, so $A_1$ is negative and the claim is a hedge.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Long-run risk premium as cash-flow leverage phi varies. The vertical line is 1/psi = 0.67, below which the claim is a hedge."
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_line, geom_vline, labs,
    theme_minimal, theme, element_blank, element_line, element_text,
)

INK, RED, GRID, BODY = "#1b1714", "#7a1f1f", "#e2d6c4", "#2d2926"
phis = [0.2 + 0.2 * i for i in range(16)]
sweep = pd.DataFrame({
    "phi": phis,
    "premium": [
        geap.LongRunRisksModel(
            claims={"mine": dict(BASE, phi=p)}
        ).solve(method="analytical").long_run_premium["mine"]
        for p in phis
    ],
})
(
    ggplot(sweep, aes("phi", "premium"))
    + geom_line(color=RED, size=0.9)
    + geom_vline(xintercept=1.0 / 1.5, color=INK, linetype="dashed", size=0.4)
    + labs(x="phi", y="long-run premium (%)")
    + theme_minimal(base_size=11)
    + theme(
        figure_size=(6.5, 3.2),
        text=element_text(color=BODY),
        panel_grid_minor=element_blank(),
        panel_grid_major=element_line(color=GRID, size=0.4),
        axis_line=element_line(color=INK, size=0.5),
    )
)
```

## Expected growth is small and persistent

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "One simulated path of expected growth x and consumption growth dc. x is a few tenths of a percent per month and moves slowly; dc is mostly transitory noise around it."
path = geap.LongRunRisksModel().simulate_paths(480, seed=3)
if not isinstance(path, pd.DataFrame):
    path = path.to_pandas()
path = path.reset_index(drop=True)
path["month"] = range(1, len(path) + 1)
long = path.melt(
    id_vars="month", value_vars=["x", "dc"],
    var_name="series", value_name="growth",
)
(
    ggplot(long, aes("month", "growth", color="series"))
    + geom_line()
    + labs(x="month", y="growth")
    + theme_minimal(base_size=11)
    + theme(
        figure_size=(6.5, 3.2),
        text=element_text(color=BODY),
        panel_grid_minor=element_blank(),
        panel_grid_major=element_line(color=GRID, size=0.4),
        axis_line=element_line(color=INK, size=0.5),
        legend_title=element_blank(),
        legend_position="top",
    )
)
```

## Loadings from 1930 to 2003 cash flows

Returns do not enter the calibration. The annual slope $\tilde\phi$ is
the estimable counterpart of monthly $\phi$. Moreover, value's slope
must come out above growth's if the paper's mechanism is correct.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

dc = pd.read_csv(DATA / "consumption_annual.csv").sort_values("year")
panel = pd.read_csv(DATA / "annual_panel.csv")
y = dc["dc"].to_numpy()

def dgrowth(claim):
    rows = panel[panel["claim"] == claim].merge(dc, on="year").sort_values("year")
    return rows["dgrowth"].to_numpy()

measured = geap.calibrate_claims(
    y,
    {"growth": dgrowth("Growth"), "value": dgrowth("Value"),
     "market": dgrowth("Market")},
    frequency="annual",
    window=2,
)
slopes = pd.DataFrame({
    "claim": list(measured),
    "phi_annual": [measured[n].phi for n in measured],
})
(
    GT(slopes)
    .tab_header(title="Annual cash-flow slopes, 1930 to 2003")
    .cols_label(claim="claim", phi_annual="annual slope")
    .fmt_number(columns="phi_annual", decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note("calibrate_claims on the shipped CSVs. Returns are not an input.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

The paper's Table VI data slopes are 0.55 (growth), 3.04 (value), and
1.26 (market). The reconstruction is inside the Table VI standard
errors, and the comparison is in `tests/test_empirical_goldens.py`. The
monthly Table II loadings are a separate object, and they are chosen so
simulated annual slopes match the data slopes.

::: {.firewall}
Table VI figures 0.55, 3.04, and 1.26 are from Kiku (2006). The table
above is computed from the shipped CSVs.
:::

## Simulated Table VII

```{python}
sim = model.simulate(n_samples=300, years=74, seed=0)
vg = sim.compare("value", "growth", market="market")
print(f"premium {vg.premium:.2f}, beta ratio {vg.beta_ratio:.2f}")
```

The paper's model column for the value premium is 5.29 (Kiku, Table
VII). A run of 300 samples is noisier than the paper's run of 1000.

Scripts under `examples/` repeat the same workflows outside the site:
`run_paper.py`, `two_firms.py`, `calibrate_any_portfolio.py`.

The source is Kiku (2006), Tables I, VI, VII, and equation (19). The
bibliography is on [References](../reference/references.qmd).
